youtube.title: Why Isn't the Night Sky Blazing White?
youtube.caption:
Why isn't the night sky blazing white? Look closely.

If space were endless and eternal, every line of sight would end on a star. Tonight's dark isn't empty: it's a clue that the universe has not been shining forever.

Series: One More Orbit · Season 2 · Episode 2.

Sources
1. In an infinite, eternal, unchanging universe every line of sight would end on a star. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/skywatching/night-sky-network/looking-beyond-the-stars-septembers-night-sky-notes/
2. Light from beyond a certain distance has not had time to reach us because the universe has a finite age. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/skywatching/night-sky-network/looking-beyond-the-stars-septembers-night-sky-notes/
3. The ESA Planck page puts the universe's age at about 13.8 billion years. — esa.int: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Planck/Planck_science_highlights
4. The dark night sky points to a universe of finite age. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/skywatching/night-sky-network/looking-beyond-the-stars-septembers-night-sky-notes/
5. Sunlight takes about 8 min 20 s to reach Earth. — science.nasa.gov: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/exoplanets/our-milky-way-galaxy-how-big-is-space/

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Sources are listed per claim; each page should be opened by a person before posting.

One More Orbit: One minute, one 'whoa' about the universe, every number sourced.
